llm.thesis: Arista is a high-quality, capital-light AI networking franchise compounding at 32.6% TTM revenue growth (accelerating ~200bps sequentially) with a 43.1% operating margin, 48.9% FCF margin, 155% ROIC, $13.3B net cash and zero debt — but the market already knows it. At 64x earnings, 23.3x EV/Sales and a 2.0% FCF yield, versus 5-year median multiples of 43.7x P/E and 14.6x EV/Sales, the shares embed continued hyperscaler AI capex and no margin erosion; the system's expectations gap of 3.0 confirms reality and pricing are near-converged. The differentiated observation is not valuation but mix: Arista is holding 43% operating margins flat while absorbing a revenue mix shift toward large AI back-end deployments that consensus has long feared would compress margins, and it is doing so with capex of only 1.4% of revenue and 1.27x FCF conversion. That argues for owning this as a cash-compounding momentum position sized for multiple compression risk, not as a value re-rating story. The asymmetric money in the AI networking constraint is more likely to be made one layer down — in optics, interconnect silicon, cooling and power — where Arista's own bill of materials is somebody else's revenue.
llm.fundamental_read: Growth is accelerating (32.6% TTM vs 30.6% prior) with FCF up 29.7% to $5.16B on just $151M of capex, i.e. an asset-light model where growth is essentially self-funding; ROIC of 155% and net debt/EBITDA of -2.9x mean the balance sheet is a $13.3B optionality reserve rather than a risk. Gross margin of 63.0% and operating margin of 43.1% were flat YoY (-0bps), so all incremental operating leverage is being reinvested — R&D is 13% of revenue and SBC 4.8%, yet diluted shares still fell 0.3% via $620M of buybacks. The one soft spot is that EPS growth (+23.9%) lags revenue growth (+32.6%), implying below-the-line or tax/interest drag rather than deteriorating unit economics. Quality score 83 is earned; the valuation score of 38 is the entire debate.
llm.technical_read: Unambiguous uptrend: price 205.7 sits above the 20/50/200-day averages (196.3/189.5/156.7), with a 50>200 configuration, positive MACD histogram and price only 2.3% below the 52-week high after +52.4% in six months. RSI at 59.5 is strong without being extended, leaving room to run, but the stock is 31.3% above its 200-day — a stretched cushion that makes it vulnerable to a fast mean-reversion air pocket on any capex headline. Key levels: the 50-day near 189 is the first defensible support; a close more than 10% below the 200-day (roughly 141) would invalidate the trend leg.
llm.market_expectation: The market expects Arista to remain the merchant-silicon-based networking standard for AI back-end and front-end fabrics, sustaining 25-30%+ growth for several years with roughly 40%+ operating margins intact despite hyperscaler pricing pressure. A 2.0% FCF yield and PEG of 2.7 imply investors are underwriting many years of durable compounding at high incremental returns and assigning little probability to either a capex digestion air pocket or share loss to alternative fabrics. With 12-month return of +43% and capital-flow score 86, positioning is consensus-long and reflexively tied to the AI capex narrative — the stock is a proxy trade, so it will discount hyperscaler spending revisions before the fundamentals show them.
what_market_misses: Flat operating margin is being read as 'no leverage,' but holding 43.1% while revenue grows 32.6% into a lower-gross-margin AI mix is arguably a positive surprise versus the long-standing bear case that hyperscaler deals would structurally dilute profitability.

EV multiples understate the quality of the balance sheet: $13.3B net cash is ~5% of market cap and zero debt, giving Arista the ability to fund M&A, aggressive buybacks or a price war without touching cash flow — an option not reflected in a 2.0% FCF yield screen.

Capital intensity is extreme in the other direction: $151M capex on $10.5B revenue (1.4%) means Arista monetizes the AI buildout without the depreciation drag that will increasingly compress reported earnings at GPU-heavy and cloud peers; FCF conversion of 1.27x is the tell.

Revenue is accelerating (+200bps sequentially) while the P/E sits at only the 60th percentile of its own 5-year range — the multiple is implicitly pricing deceleration that the latest data does not yet show.

The regime read is far weaker than the 'Goldilocks' label suggests: probabilities are near-uniform (26.6/24.6/23.5/25.4), so combined Stagflation+Contraction is ~49%. A 2.0% FCF yield asset is macro-duration exposed, and the macro signal carries almost no information — sizing should reflect that, not the label.
Shareholder yield is essentially nil (0.24%); with $13.3B of idle cash, a step-change in buyback intensity is an unpriced lever, especially since it would offset 4.8%-of-revenue SBC.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (~90 days from the 2026-08-05 filing): the swing variables are whether revenue growth holds above 30% and whether operating margin stays at/above 43%.
Hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance updates — Arista trades as a derivative of these disclosures ahead of its own results.

Evidence that AI infrastructure bottlenecks (GPU supply, power, cooling, network bandwidth) are easing, which would expand the deployable fabric base and lift the AI Infrastructure theme trend from 56 toward the levels that justify the multiple.
Continued Technology sector rotation (+66 vs all other sectors negative) sustaining the flow bid; capital-flow component already at 86.
A material acceleration of buybacks or a strategic acquisition funded from the $13.3B cash pile.
risks: Valuation: 64x P/E, 23.3x EV/Sales (vs 14.6x 5y median) and 2.0% FCF yield leave no margin for a single revenue or margin miss; a reversion to the historical median multiple alone is a very large drawdown regardless of fundamentals.

Customer concentration in a handful of hyperscalers (inferred from the business model, not in the provided data) makes revenue lumpy — one deployment pause can turn 32% growth into a stall in two quarters.
Competitive substitution in AI back-end fabrics from vertically integrated GPU-vendor networking stacks and whitebox/ODM alternatives could pressure the 63% gross margin even if revenue holds.
Crowded positioning: capital-flow score 86 and -2.3% from 52-week high mean marginal buyers are momentum-driven and will exit fast on an AI capex scare.
Macro duration risk: near-equal Stagflation/Contraction probabilities (~49% combined) against a 2.0% FCF yield means rate or liquidity shocks hit this multiple hard.
EPS growth (+23.9%) trailing revenue growth (+32.6%) — if that gap widens, the P/E denominator disappoints even with strong top line.
thesis_break_conditions: TTM revenue growth falls below 23% (currently 32.6%), signalling an AI capex digestion phase rather than a pause.
Operating margin compresses more than 200bps YoY from 43.1%, indicating hyperscaler pricing power is finally winning.
Gross margin breaks decisively below ~60% (currently 63.0%), which would mark structural mix deterioration rather than deal-specific discounting.
ROIC falls below 117% or capex intensity rises materially above ~3% of revenue, breaking the capital-light compounding story.
Price closes more than 10% below the 200-day average (~141) with negative relative strength, or the 50-day crosses below the 200-day.
Technology rotation score turns below -20 for two consecutive runs (currently +66), removing the flow support that a 64x multiple depends on.
AI Infrastructure theme trend drops below 45 (currently 56).
Diluted share count starts rising, signalling SBC is no longer being offset and management is prioritising cash hoarding over per-share value.
second_order_beneficiaries: Optical interconnect and transceiver suppliers (800G/1.6T modules, co-packaged optics): every Arista AI fabric port consumes optics, and bandwidth demand scales faster than switch unit count.

Merchant switch silicon vendors: Arista's model is built on third-party high-radix ASICs, so the silicon supplier captures the same AI fabric growth with arguably more pricing power and less customer-concentration risk than Arista itself.
Electrical interconnect, cabling and backplane/DAC suppliers serving rack-scale and scale-up fabric topologies.
Liquid cooling and thermal management vendors — switch ASIC and optics power density is rising alongside GPU density, extending cooling demand beyond the accelerator itself.

On-site power generation, grid interconnect and electrical distribution providers: the binding constraint named in the theme evidence is power availability, which gates how much networking gear can actually be energized.
HBM and advanced memory/packaging suppliers, as the accelerator side of the constraint that determines total fabric scale.
Contract manufacturers/ODMs that build the hardware Arista designs — they participate in volume growth without carrying the R&D burden or the 64x multiple.
Network test, validation and observability software vendors, whose demand scales with fabric complexity rather than with any one vendor's share.

epistemic_labels.statement: TTM revenue growth is 32.6%, accelerating from 30.6% in the prior quarter.
Operating margin is 43.1%, essentially unchanged YoY (-0bps); gross margin 63.0%; FCF margin 48.9%.
Capex was $151.3M on $10.54B revenue (1.4%), FCF $5.16B, FCF conversion 1.27x.
Balance sheet holds $13.3B cash, zero debt, net debt/EBITDA -2.9x; diluted shares down 0.3% YoY with $620M of buybacks.
Valuation is 64.1x P/E, 23.3x EV/Sales, 53.0x EV/EBITDA, 2.0% FCF yield, PEG 2.7; 5-year median EV/Sales was 14.6x and median P/E 43.7x.
Price is 2.3% below the 52-week high, 31.3% above the 200-day, RSI 59.5, MACD positive, +42.8% over 12 months.
Technology is the strongest sector on rotation (+66) while every sector except Energy is negative.
The market expects sustained high growth and intact margins, leaving little room for disappointment (expectations gap only 3.0).
Consensus has long feared that hyperscaler AI back-end deals would structurally dilute Arista's gross and operating margins.
Flat operating margin amid 32.6% growth reflects deliberate reinvestment (R&D 13% of revenue) plus AI mix, not loss of pricing power.
The 60th-percentile P/E versus accelerating revenue implies the market is discounting future deceleration.
Near-uniform regime probabilities mean the 'Goldilocks' label carries minimal information and macro risk is effectively a coin flip for a 2.0%-FCF-yield asset.
EPS growth lagging revenue growth by ~870bps points to below-the-line, tax or share-based drag rather than unit-economics deterioration.
Revenue is concentrated in a small number of hyperscale customers, making growth lumpy and headline-sensitive.
Vertically integrated GPU-vendor networking stacks and whitebox alternatives could take share in AI back-end fabrics and pressure gross margin.
A step-change in buybacks or a strategic acquisition funded from the $13.3B cash pile is an unpriced lever.
Optics, switch silicon, cooling and power suppliers capture the same AI fabric growth with potentially better risk-adjusted entry multiples.
